summary: Cyprus is an EU member but not part of the Schengen Area, so it runs its own national visa policy aligned with the EU visa-free list: EU/EEA citizens enter freely, Schengen-exempt nationalities get 90 days in any 180 (which do not count against the Schengen allowance), and holders of valid double- or multiple-entry Schengen visas can enter without a separate Cypriot visa (except Turkish and Azerbaijani citizens).

tips.text: The UK FCDO says that if you enter through the north (for example Ercan Airport), the Republic of Cyprus considers you to have entered illegally: you could be fined, refused entry to or exit from the Republic, or prevented from crossing back into the north. Entering through the south, the FCDO says you can use any crossing point between north and south, but Australia's Smartraveller says non-EU citizens are barred from the Pergamos and Strovilia crossing points, which lie in UK sovereign territory, and will be turned away.
Traffic drives on the left in Cyprus, according to Canada's travel advice. Canada adds that vehicle insurance bought in the Republic of Cyprus is not valid in the north, including for rental cars.

The UK FCDO says Cyprus is not part of the Schengen area, so visits to Cyprus do not count towards your 90-day visa-free limit in Schengen, and Schengen days do not count towards your limit in Cyprus.
Australia's Smartraveller says summer heatwaves are becoming more frequent: drink plenty of water, wear light clothing, stay in air conditioning or shade, and follow local authorities' advice.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Cyprus?
faq.answer: EU, EEA and Swiss citizens can enter with an identity card that bears their photo. Nationalities on the EU visa-free list — including the US, UK, Canada and Australia — get 90 days in any 180-day period. Others need a Cypriot national short-stay visa from a Cypriot mission, or can enter with a valid double- or multiple-entry Schengen visa (except Turkish and Azerbaijani citizens).

faq.question: Can I enter Cyprus with a Schengen visa?
faq.answer: Yes, in most cases. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs says holders of a valid double- or multiple-entry Schengen visa, or of a national visa or residence permit issued by a Schengen state, do not need a Cypriot short-stay visa for up to 90 days in any 180-day period. Turkish and Azerbaijani citizens are excluded from this rule, and a single-entry Schengen visa does not qualify.

faq.question: Do days in Cyprus count against the Schengen 90/180 limit?
faq.answer: No. Cyprus is an EU member but not part of the Schengen Area, so time spent there is counted separately from your Schengen allowance. The EU's official ETIAS website, however, lists Cyprus among the 30 European countries that will require ETIAS, and says time spent in Cyprus will be calculated separately from the 90 days allowed in the other countries; ETIAS is not yet in operation.

faq.question: Can I visit Northern Cyprus?
faq.answer: Yes, by crossing at a designated crossing point after entering through the south — Canada says crossing the UN buffer zone anywhere else is illegal. The UK FCDO says entering through the north, for example via Ercan Airport, is treated by the Republic of Cyprus as illegal entry and can lead to a fine or to being prevented from crossing back into the north.

faq.question: Which side of the road does Cyprus drive on?
faq.answer: The left. Canada's travel advice says traffic drives on the left in Cyprus. Canada adds that you must be at least 18 to drive and can use a Canadian licence for up to 6 months.
